title: Patlican Musakka
subtitle: Turkish aubergine and minced lamb bake
excerpt: Layers of fried aubergine and spiced minced lamb baked together in a tomato sauce. This is the Turkish version of musakka, without bechamel. It is rich and substantial and eats well with yoghurt and flatbread.
sourceNotes: Turkish musakka differs from the Greek version in omitting bechamel sauce. It is a common home dish across Anatolia, typically made with lamb and fried aubergine.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze fully assembled and baked. Wrap tightly and freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat from frozen at 180C until piping hot.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead and keep chilled. Bake just before serving.

content.text: Patlican musakka is a Turkish baked dish of fried aubergine and spiced lamb. Salting the aubergine before frying draws out moisture so it fries rather than absorbs oil. The dish should rest for 10 minutes before serving so the layers hold when you spoon it out.
Lay the aubergine rounds on a tray, salt generously, and leave for 20 minutes. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine rounds in batches for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden. Set aside on kitchen paper.
Heat the remaining oil in the same pan. Fry the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and green pepper and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the lamb mince and cook over high heat for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned all over.
Stir in the tomato puree, paprika, and cumin. Cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and 100 ml of water. Simmer for 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 190C. Layer half the fried aubergine in a gratin dish. Spoon over all the lamb mixture. Top with the remaining aubergine.
Bake for 25 minutes until bubbling at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes. Scatter with parsley before serving.

items.symptom: The aubergine absorbs all the oil and stays pale.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough, or the aubergine was not dried well enough.
items.fix: Pat the salted aubergine very dry and get the oil properly hot before adding. A drop of water should sizzle on contact.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin after baking.
items.cause: The tomatoes released too much liquid.
items.fix: Simmer the lamb sauce for longer before assembling. It should coat the back of a spoon before it goes into the dish.

items.symptom: The layers slide apart when served.
items.cause: It was not rested before spooning out.
items.fix: Leave it for at least 10 minutes off the heat. This allows the layers to settle and hold.
